title: Yoga: Meaning and Context
excerpt: Yoga is a family of Indian disciplines of ethics, attention, and, in many later forms, the body. A fitness class is one descendant, not the whole.

quick_answer.question: What does Yoga mean?
quick_answer.answer: Yoga names disciplined practice and philosophy. Classical lists include more than posture. Modern classes often mean posture and may be honest about that limit.

intro: Yoga is a discipline. The Yoga Sutras organize a path in which posture is one limb. The Gita uses the word for ways of acting, knowing, and devoting.

sections.heading: What does Yoga mean?
sections.content:
Hatha literature adds bodily technique. American studios add a class format. Those are three layers. Samadhi and meditation are technical neighbors, not synonyms for a stretch. The philosophy explainer follows the texts.

The neighboring page is [what yoga philosophy is](/articles/what-is-yoga-philosophy/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: Where does the word come from?
sections.content:
The Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy is a better map than a schedule of class names. NCCIH discusses yoga as a practice people use for health and warns against replacing care. Health talk and philosophy talk should not be fused.

A wider map lives at the [yoga topic](/topics/yoga/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: How is the word misused?
sections.content:
If you take a class, ask whether it is exercise, worship, or textual study. All three can be legitimate. Surprise is the problem. Read one passage if you want the philosophy.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [Hatha yoga](/yoga/hatha-yoga/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not say yoga cures disease. Do not say a weekend made you a lineage holder. Do not quote a sutra as a medical claim.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Yoga is defined here in its traditional or philosophical sense.
Popular English often widens the word until it means a mood.
Longer pages on this site carry the disagreements.

faq.question: Is Yoga a scientific term?
faq.answer: No. Yoga is a tradition and a set of practices. Some programs have been studied. The word itself is not a clinical finding.

faq.question: Where is the longer page?
faq.answer: Read the yoga pillar and the philosophy explainer.
